L110: # Current Clinical Trials
L111: We are currently seeking patients for enrollment in funded oncology clinical trials. Study goals and suitability for each patient are discussed in detail with the clients prior to enrollment.
L112: Although clinical trial enrollment may not be the best option for all patients, in many cases, clinical trial participation provides the opportunity to receive novel, cutting-edge therapies free of charge or at a reduced cost and may facilitate treatment of pets where it would not otherwise be possible due to financial constraints or lack of other therapy options. Criteria for enrollment are outlined for each tumor type below.
L113: Please direct referrals or questions to the Oncology Clinical Trials Service at 573-882-7821.
L114: Current Trials and Studies
L115: 
L116: Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BI705564) for Canine B‑Cell Lymphoma
L117: 
L118: The University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center is enrolling dogs in a clinical trial evaluating an investigational oral Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) inhibitor—BI705564—for the treatment of newly diagnosed B‑cell lymphoma. This exploratory, multicenter field study aims to assess both efficacy and safety of BTK inhibition in canine patients.
L119: 
L120: Eligibility includes:
L121:   * Dogs >1 year old and 10–50 kg in body weight
L122:   * Naïve, untreated B‑cell lymphoma confirmed by cytology or histology with immunophenotyping (flow cytometry)
L123:   * At least two peripheral lymph nodes ≥2 cm in longest diameter
L124:   * WHO stage II, III, or IV B‑cell lymphoma
L125:   * Adequate organ function on bloodwork and urinalysis
L126:   * Performance score of 0–1 (normal to mildly decreased activity) and life expectancy ≥1 month
L127:   * Owner consent
L128: 
L129: Key exclusions:
L130:   * T‑cell lymphoma or involvement of skin, GI tract, or nervous system
L131:   * Internal‑only disease (mediastinum, liver, spleen) without peripheral lymph node enlargement
L132:   * Prior lymphoma treatment (chemotherapy, Tanovea, Laverdia, radiation) or long‑term corticosteroids (>2 weeks)
L133:   * Hypercalcemia, MDR1 deficiency, pregnancy/lactation, or concurrent trial enrollment
L134: 
L135: Study overview:
L136: Dogs will receive oral BI705564 once daily for 3 months (84 days) at 5 mg/kg, with possible dose escalation to 10 mg/kg in certain cases depending on early target occupancy results.
L137: 
L138: The study includes scheduled evaluations such as:
L139: 
L140:   * Physical examinations and lymph node measurements
L141:   * Quality‑of‑life assessments
L142:   * Bloodwork (CBC, chemistry, lymphoma testing)
L143:   * Lymph node aspirates for target occupancy evaluation
L144:   * Thoracic radiographs and abdominal ultrasound at screening
L145: Follow‑up continues regularly throughout the 12‑week treatment period.
L146: 
L147: Potential benefits:
L148: 
L149:   * Access to a novel investigational BTK inhibitor designed to target B‑cell lymphoma
L150:   * All study‑related diagnostics, monitoring, and investigational drug costs are covered
L151:   * Opportunity to contribute to advancement of veterinary oncology and comparative cancer therapeutics
L152: 
L153: Potential risks:
L154:   * Possible drug‑related side effects (as with any investigational therapy)
L155:   * Risks associated with repeated lymph node aspirates, blood draws, and imaging procedures
L156:   * Dogs may be withdrawn if adverse events occur or if continued participation is not in the animal’s best interest
L157: 
L158: Owner commitment:
L159: 
L160: Owners must agree to:
L161:   * Bring their dog for all required study visits over 12 weeks
L162:   * Administer oral medication daily as directed
L163:   * Allow required diagnostic sampling (bloodwork, lymph node aspirates, imaging)
L164:   * Participate in quality‑of‑life assessments
L165: 
L166: Dogs may be withdrawn at any time. If a dog passes away during the study, postmortem evaluation is requested to improve understanding of treatment effects.
L167: 
L168: Contact
L169: For more information on this study please contact:
L170: 📧 cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu
L171: Please include the subject line: BI705564 BTK Inhibitor Trial
L172: 
L173: COTC033: Repurposing Vaccine Immunity to Treat Cancers
L174: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of a new immunotherapy, the Vaccine Peptide Library (VPL), when given to dogs with cancer. Studies in dogs with cancer will complement current human trials designed to test new doses and effects of this agent.
L175: 
L176: Criteria:
L177:   * Body weight between 15 and 60 kg
L178:   * Tumor biopsy or cytology to confirm diagnosis
L179:   * Solid tumor measuring 2 to 8 cm
L180:   * No mast cell tumors, cutaneous hemangiosarcomas, thyroid carcinomas, or lymphomas
L181:   * Must not have received ANY prior experimental therapy
L182:   * No concurrent chemotherapy or radiation therapy – 2 week washout period required
L183:   * No concurrent immunomodulatory therapy (including Apoquel or Cytopoint) – 6 week washout period required
L184:   * No concurrent corticosteroids – 1 week washout period required
L185:   * No hypercalcemia causing illness
L186:   * No significant co-morbid illness, which includes, but is not limited to: pulmonary metastatic disease, renal or hepatic failure, history of congestive heart failure or clinical coagulopathy, autoimmune disorders, or uncontrolled endocrinopathies
L187: Benefit:
L188: 
L189:   * Complete cost of all treatments and rechecks covered by study, include initial staging or adverse side effects.
L190:   * This trial is being conducted concurrently with human trials.
L191:   * Contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L192:   * At the conclusion of the study, there will be a $1000 monetary gift provided towards additional treatment for your pet’s cancer.
L193: 
L194: To Participate:
L195:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L196:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L197:   * Participation will require a total of up to 13 weekly visits.
L198: 
L199: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【70†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L200: Gilvetmab for the Treatment of Primary Pulmonary Carcinoma in Dogs
L201: 
L202: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the effectiveness of Gilvetmab, an anti-PD1 monoclonal antibody, as a treatment for canine pulmonary carcinoma. Similar treatments have been shown to improve survival in human lung cancer patients.
L203: 
L204: Criteria:
L205:   * Dogs with gross disease and those with microscopic disease
L206:   * No immune-mediated disease or other severe comorbidities
L207:   * No concurrent use of steroids or other immunosuppressive drugs
L208: 
L209: Study Involvement:
L210: 
L211:   * Gilvetmab is given as a slow infusion every two weeks for up to 10 doses.
L212:   * CBC, chemistry, and urinalysis are performed every 4 weeks.
L213:   * Chest x-rays are performed every 8 weeks.
L214: 
L215: Benefit:
L216:   * The study covers the cost of Gilvetmab treatment (ranges from $540 – $1350 per treatment, depending on patient size).
L217:   * Owner is responsive for recheck exams, bloodwork, and x-rays.
L218: 
L219: To Participate:
L220: 
L221:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, MO for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L222:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L223:   * Participation will require a total of up to 10 biweekly visits.
L224: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest 【71†or fill out a short survey here.†missouri.qualtrics.com】
L225: 
L226: LEAH xCAR-T: Canine B-Cell Lymphoma
L227: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of lymphodepleting chemotherapy and xenogenic CAR-T cell therapy in dogs with spontaneous CD20+ lymphoma. CAR-T cells are lymphocytes (immune cells) that have had a series of genes added to them that make them professional killers of any cell carrying the target molecule.
L228: This study will seek to better understand the effects of the CAR-T cells on the tumor as well as the dog’s immune system.
L229: Criteria:
L230: 
L231:   * Canine patients weighing over 10kg
L232: 
L233:   * Patients with naive (newly diagnosed) and relapsed (pre-treated) Large Cell B-Cell lymphoma.
L234: 
L235:   * Must be feeling clinically WELL at home.
L236: 
L237:   * Must meet bloodwork requirements and have no evidence of primary gastrointestinal or lung involvement; eligibility is at the discretion of the investigator.
L238:   * Patients CANNOT be receiving immunomodulatory drugs (Apoquel, mycophenolate, cyclosporine, azathioprine).
L239:   * Patients must be off prednisone for a minimum of 72 hours prior to CAR-T therapy.
L240: 
L241: Benefit:
L242: 
L243:   * Complete cost of all treatments and rechecks are covered by study, including initial staging; up to $4,000 allotted for possible adverse events; $2,000 stipend for additional/future treatment at the VHC upon completion
L244: 
L245:   * You pet will contribute to development of an important cancer therapy.
L246: To Participate:
L247: 
L248:   * Pet owners must be willing to transport their dog to and from the treatment center in Columbia, Missouri, for every visit abiding by specific timelines.
L249: 
L250:   * A full screening will be performed prior to full study enrollment.
L251: 
L252:   * Participation will require pets to come to our clinic for a minimum of seven visits over the first 21 days of the study, with future longer-term follow up appointments required, and/or until progression or relapse.
L253: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.
L254: 
L255: Thyroid Sodium Iodide Symporter
L256: The University of Missouri Veterinary Medical Center is enrolling patients into a clinical trial to assess whether using special stains for the sodium iodide symporter can allow us to identify tumors that are taking up iodine after a thyroid tumor has been removed. This would limit the need for expensive thyroid scans before surgery and increase the number of dogs that could be considered for additional treatment if their thyroid cancer is aggressive.
L257: 
L258: Criteria:
L259:   * Dogs with presumed thyroid carcinoma considered likely candidates for thyroidectomy
L260:   * Patients who have received neoadjuvant radiation (external beam or I-131) or chemotherapy, exogenous iodine supplementation are not eligible.
L261: 
L262: Benefit:
L263:   * The pre-operative thyroid scan would allow radioactive iodine therapy to be considered as an option following surgery, if there were concerns that your dog’s thyroid tumor was more aggressive than usual.
L264:   * After enrollment, the study will contribute $1,500 to cover associated clinical costs. This includes coverage of costs associated with the pre-operative thyroid scan, including sedation and hospital care (approximately ($1,055).
L265: 
L266: To Participate:
L267:   * Pet owners must be willing to move forward with surgical planning and resection of thyroid and surrounding lymph nodes.
L268:   * A full screening will be performed prior to enrollment at the owner’s expense.
L269:     * Responsible for initial assessment and consultation to determine eligibility for the trial.
L270: 
L271: For more information on this study please contact: cvmclinicaltrials@missouri.edu with the subject pertaining to the trial of interest.
